external_input.reason: The library exposes public application-workload entrypoints: Node.Propose and Node.ProposeConfChange (and RawNode equivalents) accept proposals and membership changes originating outside the protocol and convert them to internal MsgProp messages. Peer-to-peer message ingress (Step) and timer events (Tick) are separate APIs and are excluded as required.
limitations: Only the protocol library is in scope; the application-facing transport and retry layers that feed Propose are outside the boundary.
Proposals can be dropped or forwarded (stepFollower raft.go:1715-1724); the API contract documents this.

evidence.reason: Explicit stop boundary: stops the run loop, closes done, and all later calls return ErrStopped (node.go:34-35).
Existing recovery path: creates a node whose state is restored from Storage instead of a peer list.
Recovery reads InitialState from Storage, restores HardState via loadState (raft.go:2033) and applies Config.Applied (raft.go:482-484).
SoftState documented as volatile, not persisted to the WAL.

lifecycle_control.boundary: In-module Storage interface and MemoryStorage are inside the boundary; durable WAL/disk and process supervision are outside.
lifecycle_control.reason: The library already defines the persistent/volatile split (HardState must be persisted, SoftState is volatile, MustSync decision), provides a restart path (RestartNode/newRaft reads Storage.InitialState, Config.Applied, loadState), owns its recoverable state, and exposes an explicit stop boundary (Node.Stop with ErrStopped semantics). No state-survival decision must be invented by an Agent.
limitations: Crash durability is delegated to the application's Storage implementation; the shipped MemoryStorage is in-memory only, so cross-process crash survival requires an external WAL (outside the boundary).
Restarting a stopped node means constructing a new Node from Storage; there is no in-process resume of a stopped Node.

evidence.reason: HardState documented as state to be saved to stable storage before messages are sent.

persistent_volatile_semantics_defined.reason: Ready contract (node.go:49-114) explicitly states HardState/Entries/Snapshot must be saved to stable storage before messages are sent, SoftState is volatile (node.go:38-43), and MustSync (rawnode.go:191-200) codifies durability requirements.

This is an explicit restart path; it is not a scheduler resume.

evidence.reason: Single message-creation/scheduling point: fills From/Term and appends to r.msgs or r.msgsAfterAppend.
Ready.Messages = r.msgs plus msgsAfterAppend and (async mode) MsgStorageAppend/MsgStorageApply; the point where all outbound messages become visible before any transport send.
Ready (including Messages) is produced and handed to the application via readyc; no library-side send exists.

Async-storage local messages (MsgStorageAppend/MsgStorageApply targeting LocalAppendThread/LocalApplyThread, raft.go:40-44) are also appended to Messages and must be distinguished by a capture controller.

message_capture.boundary: Capture point is inside the library (Ready.Messages generation); the actual network send occurs in the application transport outside the boundary.
message_capture.gap: A test-mode capture controller must be added: intercept Ready.Messages (the single outbound choke point) or wrap raft.send, copy pb.Message values into a stable pending snapshot with CaptureSequence, and suppress application-side forwarding of captured messages.
message_capture.reason: No test-mode message controller exists (no MessageController/CaptureSequence anywhere in the module). However, message creation is centralized in raft.send (raft.go:512-599) which appends to r.msgs / r.msgsAfterAppend, and every outbound protocol message is handed to the application in a single choke point, Ready.Messages (rawnode.go:141-189, node.go:368/440). A capture controller can be added there, before any application transport send; suppression is achievable because the library itself never sends — the 'uncontrollable send path' is the application transport outside the boundary.
limitations: Heartbeats (tickHeartbeat raft.go:862 -> MsgBeat -> sendHeartbeat raft.go:692), append retries (maybeSendAppend raft.go:616), snapshots (maybeSendSnapshot raft.go:664, MsgSnap with ReportSnapshot contract rawnode.go:108-110), forwarded proposals (stepFollower raft.go:1715-1724) and async-storage local messages (rawnode.go:165-186) all flow through the same Ready.Messages choke point, so a capture implemented there covers them uniformly.
Suppression of the real network send must be honored by the application transport (outside the boundary) or by withholding captured messages from it.
MsgsAfterAppend (vote/app responses, raft.go:590) are only appended to Ready.Messages in non-async mode (rawnode.go:176-186); capture must cover both modes.
message_capture.suggested_direction: Add a controller that wraps RawNode.Ready / Node.Ready (or hooks readyWithoutAccept), deep-copies Ready.Messages into a pending store with capture sequence IDs, and removes captured messages from what the application may forward.

message_injection.boundary: Delivery is in-process via the target node's Step; no network transport exists or is required inside the boundary.
message_injection.gap: Implement a controller that stores captured messages, selects by message ID, and delivers them by invoking the recorded target's Step (async for Node, sync for RawNode); propagate Step errors and keep the message pending on failure.
message_injection.reason: No injection controller exists, but the normal protocol input boundary is unambiguous and deterministic in-process: Node.Step (node.go:478), RawNode.Step (rawnode.go:118) and raft.Step (raft.go:1085). A controller can deliver a captured pb.Message unchanged through the recorded target's Step (target selected by the message's To field), which preserves sender, receiver, and content. Step already returns errors (ErrStepLocalMsg, ErrStepPeerNotFound, rawnode.go:24-29) that a failed Inject can propagate while leaving the message pending. This is not INVASIVE_REDISCOVERED because Step is an existing deterministic target binding that needs no caller setup.
limitations: Node.Step delivery is asynchronous (channel-based, node.go:513-550); deterministic tests should prefer RawNode.Step or wait for completion.
Self-addressed and local messages are rejected by Step (node.go:479-483, rawnode.go:119-126); only previously captured legal peer messages can be injected.
Multi-node global ordering is the test harness's concern; the library provides per-node input only.
message_injection.suggested_direction: Add a pending-message controller (per test session) that captures Ready.Messages, assigns message IDs, and injects by calling target.Step/RawNode.Step with the stored pb.Message unchanged.

evidence.reason: Step exists as the delivery primitive, but nothing selects or delivers pending captured messages.

inject.reason: No Inject(messageID) API exists; no controller holds captured messages to deliver.

delivery_binding.reason: No Transport abstraction exists to wrap (search for 'type Transport' returns nothing), but an existing deterministic in-process target binding is available: calling the recorded target's Step/RawNode.Step directly with the captured message, as the shipped rafttest harness already does (rafttest delivers queued messages to RawNode.Step; InteractionEnv.Messages queue, interaction_env.go:52). A controller needs no additional caller-provided transport.

evidence.reason: Random source wrapper using crypto/rand.Reader; no seed/injection hook.
Package-global rand; only consumer is the election timeout.
Election timeout randomization; sole protocol randomness use.
Existing determinism only via direct internal field mutation in same-package tests; not a public API.
Test-harness-only plumbing that directly sets the field; not part of the library API.

randomness_control.boundary: Randomness is fully inside the library (single global source, single consumer).
randomness_control.gap: No injectable/fixable random source exists in the public API; globalRand must be made settable (e.g., configurable source) to make the same initial state and seed produce repeatable election timeouts.
randomness_control.reason: The only protocol-relevant randomness is the randomized election timeout, computed at resetRandomizedElectionTimeout (raft.go:2049-2051) via globalRand (raft.go:102), a lockedRand backed by crypto/rand.Reader (raft.go:88-100). There is no public seeding or injection API; determinism is currently only achievable by same-package tests mutating r.randomizedElectionTimeout directly (raft_test.go:4093) or via the rafttest option plumbing (interaction_env.go:31-33). The change is localized to the rand source, so it is patchable.
limitations: crypto/rand is intentionally non-deterministic; repeatability requires an injected PRNG.
rafttest's SetRandomizedElectionTimeout bypasses the random source entirely and is test-support only.
randomness_control.suggested_direction: Introduce an injectable rand source (config field or setter) used by resetRandomizedElectionTimeout, defaulting to the current crypto-backed source.

evidence.reason: Explicit tick increments the internal logical clock; election and heartbeat timeouts are in tick units.
Synchronous tick advance for RawNode.
Election timeout measured purely in elapsed ticks; no timers or wall clock.
Heartbeat cadence measured purely in elapsed ticks.
Config documents timeouts as numbers of Node.Tick invocations.

time_control.boundary: Time is advanced explicitly by the caller; the library never reads a clock.
time_control.reason: The protocol is fully tick-driven: Node.Tick (node.go:463), RawNode.Tick (rawnode.go:64) and RawNode.TickQuiesced (rawnode.go:78) advance logical time; ElectionTick/HeartbeatTick are defined in tick units (raft.go:128-138) and consumed by tickElection/tickHeartbeat (raft.go:850-889). There is no wall-clock usage in the library (no time.Now/time.Timer/time.After anywhere in non-test source), and no ForceTimeout/ForceElection API exists, satisfying the explicit_tick accepted form.
limitations: A test harness must drive Tick at its own pace; the library provides no timer source.
The rafttest package's own harness uses real time for its network driver (rafttest/network.go), but that is outside the library's protocol time model.
